title: Three Mornings and One Short Neck
subtitle: 动物世界 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物与植物）
meta: 主题语境：动物世界（人与自然·自然生态·动物与植物）　|　核心词汇：giraffe　|　正文 342 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 giraffe 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1966 the keeper ① fed a giraffe that no visitor in the park would have described, and he said the feeding was the whole of the morning. The ② giraffe, meaning the animal itself and not the picture, ran three mornings and stayed undescribed in the book; a giraffe, he said, is the only thing in a park that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ giraffe in that park had the same short neck beside it, and the ④ giraffe at the far tree, meaning the one they kept for the children and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A giraffe, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the keeper said the describing is the part that fills three mornings.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the giraffe was the whole of the matter, meaning the height and not the animal. The ⑥ giraffe, meaning the height and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; giraffe, he said, is either something you feed or the only word that means both an animal and a height. He said the height is the part they remember.

By 1971 the ⑦ giraffe had become a line in a plan, and the plan had become an argument about the short neck. The ⑧ giraffe of the whole thing, the keeper wrote in November, was one park and three mornings of describing; giraffe, he said, is either the one at the far tree or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ giraffe I remember is the one described in the plan, which closed in 1973 and is still described as the quietest in the park. A ⑩ giraffe, my mother said in 1975, is the only one that improves by being described; every giraffe, she said, is a height that has agreed to look like an animal. She said the height was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 长颈鹿（指园里每一只旁边的那一只）
B. n. 长颈鹿（指那只动物本身，与图画相对）
C. 固定搭配：feed a giraffe 喂一只长颈鹿
D. n. 长颈鹿（指留给孩子们看的那一只）
E. n. 长颈鹿（抽象总称，指一处园子的长颈鹿之事）
F. n. 长颈鹿（指方案里写到、被记录过的那一只）
G. n. 高个子；高度（指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 高度（抽象总称，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: feed a giraffe 意为“喂一只长颈鹿”，1966 年那位饲养员喂了园子里没有一位游客肯描述的一只长颈鹿。
giraffe 意为“长颈鹿”，指那只动物本身而不是图画，它经过了三个早晨而在簿子上没有被描述。
giraffe 意为“长颈鹿”，指园里每一只旁边的那一只，每一只旁边都有同一截矮矮的脖子。
giraffe 意为“长颈鹿”，指最远那棵树旁留给孩子们看的那一只，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
giraffe 意为“高度”，指一件事里人人都看却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个高度就是那件事的全部。
giraffe 意为“高度”，指人人都看却无人提起的那样东西而不是那只长颈鹿，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
giraffe 意为“长颈鹿”，指方案里写到、被记录过的那一只，到 1971 年这一只成了方案里的一行。
giraffe 意为“长颈鹿”，饲养员十一月写道，整件事的长颈鹿之事是一处园子和三个早晨的描述。
giraffe 意为“长颈鹿”，我记得的是方案里描述过的那一只，1973 年离开了，至今仍被说成园子里最安静的一只。
giraffe 为抽象总称，母亲 1975 年说，一只长颈鹿是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的东西。
